status: written on 2026-10-24 (issue #64, RF-9) from the 334 readable intents of the pilot's two paid runs (llm_negotiation/runs/rf_pilot and rf_pilot_v2); replaces intent_v1, the draft written before any model reply. Never edited once a result rests on it: a change is intent_v3.
description: Codes the free-text `intent` of a reply (docs/resolution.md, D1) into strategy categories by keywords, with no LLM. Patterns are Python regular expressions, matched case-insensitively. An intent may take several categories. `carry_on` is kept only when no other category matched ('move left and walk on' is keep_to_side). An intent that matches nothing is `other`, never forced into a category.

side.description: The side the agent says it will move to. Only phrases about the agent's own movement count; a side said of the other person ('let them pass on my right') makes the side unknown, and a sentence naming both sides too. intent_v2: any form of a movement verb, with or without 'my' or 'the'; and the side the other is let pass on ('let her pass on my left') names the agent's own side as the opposite one.

changes_from_v1: slow_down: a negated slowing ('without slowing', 'not slowing', 'no need to slow') is not slowing; v1 coded 'Keep walking ... without slowing' as slow_down.
keep_to_side: 'to my side' / 'on my side of the passage', 'sidestep', 'step(ping) aside' added; the model says 'keep to my side' far more often than v1's 'to one side'.
carry_on: 'keep heading', 'keep straight', 'keep / stay my course', 'hold(ing) my line', 'at my normal / steady pace', 'without slowing' added.

side: a movement verb in any form ('shifting', 'easing', 'edging', 'angling', 'steering', 'sticking', 'favouring') with or without 'my' or 'the' before the side ('easing slightly right'); v1 needed the bare verb and 'my' or 'the', and read no side from 141 of the 334 intents that name one.

side: the side the other is let pass on ('let her pass on my left', 'so the older man can pass on my left') names the agent's own side as the opposite one. 'I pass X on my right' is not read: in the pilot it meant 'I go right' in 3 of 4 cases where the plan turned, so it is ambiguous.

keep_to_side: giving room ('give / giving / making / leave room', 'space to pass', 'a wide berth', 'keep(ing) clear of', 'out of the way'). In the pilot, 51 of the 54 intents that give room without naming a side came with a turn in the plan; under v2 without them, they were the commonest 'mismatch' (intent 'carry on', plan turns).
